question:
A 14-year-old boy newly enrolled in your practice presents with no current health complaints. His
parents report a notable family history of intestinal polyps on his father’s side. He denies noticing any
blood in his stool. On examination, his vital signs are as follows: heart rate of 80 beats per minute,
blood pressure of 106/72 mm Hg, respiratory rate of 19 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of
98% on room air. He has anicteric sclerae and freckles around his mouth. His abdominal examination
reveals a soft, nontender, and nondistended abdomen. Rectal examination shows no fissures, tags, or
hemorrhoids. Which condition is this patient most likely to develop by the age of 18? Answer Choices:
(A) Malignant melanoma (B) Intussusception (C) Small bowel obstruction (D) Gastrointestinal bleeding
(E) Bowel infarction (F) Mesenteric ischemia (G) Intestinal perforation (H) Longitudinal melanonychia
(I) Colonic volvulus (J) Colon cancer
 A. Mesenteric ischemia
B. Intussusception
C. Colonic volvulus
D. Longitudinal melanonychia
E. Small bowel obstruction
F. Malignant melanoma
G. Bowel infarction
H. Intestinal perforation
I. Colon cancer
J. Gastrointestinal bleeding
